subject: PayGrid model-fit eval / parity thresholds and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: PayGrid model-fit eval / parity thresholds and next steps

Hi Samir —

Great to meet earlier. Short recap and next steps so we're all aligned: 

Call recap:
- Your main objective: embed Redwood to serve PayGrid's customer-facing chat and intent extraction with parity to your in-house baseline (PayGrid Baseline v2). Latency target: p95 < 250ms for single-threaded requests; cost target: < $0.002/token average.
- Primary evaluation axis: intent classification F1 on the PayGrid test set and downstream slot-fill accuracy.
- Risk: quality regressions on edge-case prompts (account linking, refund policies).

What we propose next (action items):
1) Redwood runs an initial model-fit eval on your sample prompts + test set using 3 candidate model variants (we'll run open models and our tuned quantized variants). Deliverable: CSV with per-example verdicts and aggregated metrics.
2) Define acceptance thresholds — e.g., intent F1 within 2% absolute of PayGrid Baseline v2, and no more than 5% drop on critical intents.
3) Exchange prompt sets (you gave the initial 1k sample; please confirm we can use it).
4) Schedule a 30-min sync to review results the week of Sep 7 — propose Tue 9/8 or Wed 9/9.

Attachments & links:
- Attached: paygrid_eval_results_v1.csv (skeleton with columns we will populate), prompt_set_v3.md (format we expect), model_recommendations.pdf (high-level).
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/PG-2026-09-01

Questions for you before we start:
- Confirm we can use the provided 1k prompt set for offline evaluation.
- Any must-pass intents or regulatory constraints we should know about?

Thanks — we'll start the runs as soon as you confirm.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Samir Shah <samir@paygrid.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit eval / parity thresholds and next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap.

We confirm the 1k prompt sample can be used for the offline run. A couple quick clarifications: 
- Parity definition: our internal ask is that open models are within 2% absolute F1 of our Baseline v2 across the full test set, but critically we want no more than 3% absolute drop on our top 10 high-impact intents (billing, chargeback, refund, subscription-change, cancel). If we see regressions on those, we need mitigation plans (e.g., prompt engineering, reranking, fallback to Baseline).
- Proprietary baseline: our Baseline v2 was trained with in-domain signals and some user-history features (we will strip PII). Will Redwood compare on both raw model-only predictions and a pipeline where you simulate our upstream features?

Also, curious about which open models you plan to evaluate — can you share the list and a rough expectation of latency/quantized footprint?

Samir
Samir Shah
Head of AI, PayGrid
samir@paygrid.com

Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit eval / parity thresholds and next steps

Thanks for the clear constraints, Samir — that helps. Answers below plus proposed evaluation plan.

Quick answers:
- Models we'll evaluate (initial sweep):
  * Llama-3-70B-Chat (quantized INT8, Redwood-tuned) — strong chat/intent extraction baseline; expected p95 latency ~220ms on our reserved GPU profile, model footprint ~18GB quantized.
  * Falcon-180B-Instruct (quantized Q4_0) — high-quality few-shot reasoning on edge cases; expected p95 ~260ms, footprint ~24GB.
  * Mistral-Instruct-65B (RNNA optimized path) — good tradeoff latency/quality, p95 ~200ms, footprint ~16GB.
  * Redwood Hybrid Baseline (our tuned open variant with light prompt augmentation) — intended to approximate your Baseline v2 with prompt scaffolding and reranker enabled.

- Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
  * Overall intent F1 >= (Baseline v2 F1 - 2.0% absolute).
  * Top-10 high-impact intents: no more than 3.0% absolute drop.
  * Slot-fill exact match: within 2.5% absolute.
  * Regression guardrail: if >5% of examples for any intent flip from correct->incorrect compared to Baseline, we mark as unacceptable.

Proposed evaluation flow (we'll run and share per-example CSV + aggregate metrics):
1) Baseline run: run your Baseline v2 predictions on the shared test set so we have direct comparison. (If you can't share the model, please share the baseline predictions CSV.)
2) Model sweep: run the four candidate variants above on the same test set + prompt set.
3) Edge-case analysis: generate a short list of examples where models diverge and annotate root cause (prompt sensitivity, hallucination, tokenization differences).
4) Mitigation experiments: for any failed intents, we'll try prompt reworks, reranking, and a small lightweight adapter (if allowed) to close the gap.

Attachments: I've uploaded a starter results skeleton to the Drive and attached the prompt_set_v3.md to show input formatting. We'll populate paygrid_eval_results_v1.csv and share a full report.

Timing & next steps:
- We'll start runs tomorrow (Thu 9/3) and aim to have initial results by EOD Mon 9/7.
- Propose a results review Wed 9/9 10:00am PT — please confirm.

If you're okay with the thresholds above, we'll proceed. If you want tighter parity, call that out and we'll include a mitigation-run budget in the proposal.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachment(s): prompt_set_v3.md
